entry.title: From sounds to sentences: A longitudinal study of phonological and emergent literacy predictors of early writing in Turkish children

link.title: From sounds to sentences: A longitudinal study of phonological and emergent literacy predictors of early writing in Turkish children
(PDF) From sounds to sentences: A longitudinal study of phonological and emergent literacy predictors of early writing in Turkish children
(XML) From sounds to sentences: A longitudinal study of phonological and emergent literacy predictors of early writing in Turkish children

entry.content:
by Aysel Ferah Özcan, Hilal İlknur Tunçeli

This longitudinal study examines how preschool children’s phonological awareness and emergent literacy skills relate to their early writing performance in first grade. Conducted within the context of a transparent Turkish orthography, the study aims to identify early cognitive-linguistic correlates of subsequent writing development. A total of 97 children (aged 66–77 months) from preschools in a socioeconomically diverse Turkish district were followed over two academic years. In the first year, participants were assessed using the LAP-3 Early Literacy Subtest and the Phonological Awareness Test to measure their emergent literacy and phonological skills. One year later, their writing performance was evaluated using a validated sentence construction assessment. Non-parametric statistical tests and correlation analyses were conducted to examine developmental variations and relationships among the variables. Results revealed statistically significant correlations between early writing performance and both phonological awareness (r = .46, p < .01) and emergent literacy (r = .32, p < .01). Specific sub-skills such as syllable segmentation, rhyming awareness, and letter-sound correspondence showed the strongest associations with writing performance. These skills did not differ significantly by age or gender. The findings highlight the foundational role of preschool phonological and emergent literacy skills in early writing development. This study contributes empirical data from a transparent orthography. Given the correlational design, these findings should be interpreted as evidence consistent with developmental literacy theories rather than as confirmation of causal or predictive mechanisms; they emphasize the importance of early identification and instructional support in preschool settings to promote future writing success.

entry.title: The antibacterial and antifungal activity of honey and propolis from the Australian stingless bee Tetragonula carbonaria

link.title: The antibacterial and antifungal activity of honey and propolis from the Australian stingless bee Tetragonula carbonaria
(PDF) The antibacterial and antifungal activity of honey and propolis from the Australian stingless bee Tetragonula carbonaria
(XML) The antibacterial and antifungal activity of honey and propolis from the Australian stingless bee Tetragonula carbonaria

entry.content:
by Jasmin Li, Rosalyn Gloag, Dee A. Carter, Kenya E. Fernandes

The global rise of antimicrobial-resistant pathogens has increased interest in bee-derived natural products as sources of novel antimicrobials. While most research has focused on European honey bee (Apis mellifera) products, the 550 species of stingless bees found globally also produce honey and other hive products, representing a largely unexplored source of novel bioactives. This study investigates the antimicrobial activity of propolis extracts and honey from the Australian stingless bee Tetragonula carbonaria against 16 clinically significant bacterial and fungal pathogens, using broth microdilution methodology. T. carbonaria propolis and honey exhibited distinct antimicrobial profiles: propolis showed selective activity against a subset of bacteria and certain filamentous fungi, while honey showed broad-spectrum activity against all tested bacteria and selective activity against dermatophyte fungi. The level of H2O2 production in T. carbonaria honey was only moderately correlated with its antimicrobial activity, and the total phenolic content of propolis did not correlate significantly with its antimicrobial activity, suggesting other bee- or plant-derived compounds are important contributors. These findings highlight T. carbonaria propolis and honey as promising antimicrobials and potential sources of novel bioactive compounds.

entry.title: Single-cell analysis of COPD: Microenvironmental interactions driven by immune-fibrotic imbalance

link.title: Single-cell analysis of COPD: Microenvironmental interactions driven by immune-fibrotic imbalance
(PDF) Single-cell analysis of COPD: Microenvironmental interactions driven by immune-fibrotic imbalance
(XML) Single-cell analysis of COPD: Microenvironmental interactions driven by immune-fibrotic imbalance

entry.content:
by Hong Jiang, Wenxing Wang, Lu Wang, Jiaojian Wu, Jianjiang Luo, Qi Yan, Xueli Gong, Jing Liang

Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a respiratory disease with a high degree of cellular heterogeneity and molecular complexity, characterized pathologically by persistent airflow limitation and an inflammatory-tissue remodeling cascade involving multiple cell types. Traditional transcriptomics lack the resolution to precisely define cell subpopulation roles in COPD. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) overcomes this limitation by enabling high-resolution analysis of cell-type-specific mechanisms in COPD. A total of 101,009 cells from three scRNA-seq datasets were integrated to profile COPD-related molecular features and cell interactions at single-cell resolution. Analysis identified four major cell types and 17 distinct cell subtypes. Cell–cell communication analysis revealed a significant reduction in signaling activity of macrophages and fibroblasts, whereas certain immune cells exhibited enhanced signaling, suggesting that immune dysregulation plays a pivotal role in COPD pathogenesis. Further analysis focused on macrophage-dominant myeloid cells and fibroblasts, uncovering their critical roles in inflammation modulation and fibrosis progression. Meanwhile, this study also identified 19 chemicals that may influence COPD progression by modulating cellular gene expression. This study provides an important molecular basis for unraveling the cell-cell interaction network of COPD and elucidating the mechanism of each cell subpopulation in the disease process.

entry.title: Epidemiological characterization of avian influenza virus circulation in pigeons and quail across different production systems in Chattogram, Bangladesh

link.title: Epidemiological characterization of avian influenza virus circulation in pigeons and quail across different production systems in Chattogram, Bangladesh
(PDF) Epidemiological characterization of avian influenza virus circulation in pigeons and quail across different production systems in Chattogram, Bangladesh
(XML) Epidemiological characterization of avian influenza virus circulation in pigeons and quail across different production systems in Chattogram, Bangladesh

entry.content:
by Mohammad Iqbal Habib, Md Abu Sayeed, Monjurul Islam, Mohammad Ferdous Rahman Sarker, Sydus Shalekin Shakil, Mohammad Mahmudul Hassan, Jade K. Forwood, Abdul Ahad, Ariful Islam

Pigeons and quail contribute to poultry production, nutrition, and livelihoods in Bangladesh; however, their role in avian influenza virus (AIV) circulation remains poorly understood. These poultry species are widely reared and traded alongside chickens and ducks in household farms, commercial systems, and live bird markets, where inadequate biosecurity may create an overlooked ecological niche for AIV circulation, reassortment, and potential zoonotic spillover. Between November 2021 and April 2022, we conducted a cross-sectional study in Chattogram, Bangladesh, to estimate the prevalence and subtype-specific distribution of AIV and to identify factors associated with AIV positivity in pigeons and quail. A total of 300 birds (108 pigeons and 192 quail) were sampled from households, commercial farms, and live bird markets. Oropharyngeal and cloacal swabs were collected from each bird and tested for the AIV matrix gene using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, followed by subtype-specific detection of H5, H7, and H9. Data collected from bird owners and traders included bird demographic characteristics, bird source, and health status using a structured questionnaire. The overall prevalence of AIV was 14.3% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 10.6–18.8). Quail had a higher prevalence (18.2%, 95% CI: 13.0–24.4) than pigeons (7.4%, 95% CI: 3.3–14.1). Among detected subtypes, H9 was most prevalent (11.3%, 95% CI: 7.9–15.4), followed by hemagglutinin (HA)-untyped (2.7%, 95% CI: 1.2–5.1) and H5 (0.3%, 95% CI: 0.001–1.8), while H7 was not detected. Quail had higher odds of AIV positivity than pigeons (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 4.1, 95% CI: 1.8–10.6); clinically sick birds (aOR = 2.9, 95% CI: 1.4–6.2) and birds sampled from household farms (aOR = 2.8, 95% CI: 1.2–6.5) also had higher odds of AIV positivity. These findings indicate that pigeons and quails, which are understudied poultry species, may contribute to the maintenance and transmission of AIV within mixed poultry production and marketing systems in Bangladesh. Integrating these species into routine AIV surveillance is therefore necessary to strengthen early detection, inform control strategies, and reduce the risk of zoonotic spillover.

entry.title: The combination of simethicone and N-acetylcysteine in lidocaine ice popsicle compared with lidocaine ice popsicle alone in patients undergoing unsedated esophagogastroduodenoscopy: A prospective double-blind randomized controlled trial

link.title: The combination of simethicone and N-acetylcysteine in lidocaine ice popsicle compared with lidocaine ice popsicle alone in patients undergoing unsedated esophagogastroduodenoscopy: A prospective double-blind randomized controlled trial

(PDF) The combination of simethicone and N-acetylcysteine in lidocaine ice popsicle compared with lidocaine ice popsicle alone in patients undergoing unsedated esophagogastroduodenoscopy: A prospective double-blind randomized controlled trial

(XML) The combination of simethicone and N-acetylcysteine in lidocaine ice popsicle compared with lidocaine ice popsicle alone in patients undergoing unsedated esophagogastroduodenoscopy: A prospective double-blind randomized controlled trial

entry.content:
by Pailin Intarasangkhanawin, Saritphat Orrapin, Worapong Anuponganan, Neranchala Soonthornkes, Prasit Mahawongkajit

Background

Optimal mucosal visualization is essential for high-quality esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD), particularly for the detection of subtle upper gastrointestinal lesions. Oral simethicone and N-acetylcysteine (NAC) are commonly used to improve mucosal cleanliness, whereas lidocaine ice popsicles provide effective topical pharyngeal anesthesia for unsedated EGD. We evaluated whether incorporating simethicone and NAC into a lidocaine ice popsicle could improve mucosal visibility while maintaining patient comfort.

Methods

This single-center, prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled trial enrolled 374 adults undergoing unsedated diagnostic EGD between December 2024 and June 2025. Participants were randomized (1:1) to receive either a lidocaine ice popsicle containing simethicone (100 mg) and NAC (600 mg) or a conventional lidocaine ice popsicle. The primary outcome was mucosal visibility assessed using a modified Total Visibility Score (TVS). Secondary outcomes included procedure time, water volume required for mucosal cleansing, additional simethicone use, endoscopist satisfaction, ease of esophageal instrumentation, gag reflex, patient satisfaction, discomfort, pain, and adverse events. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 25.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA).

Results

All 374 randomized participants (187 per group) completed the study and were analyzed according to their assigned groups. Baseline characteristics were descriptively similar between groups. The intervention group had a significantly lower TVS than the control group (6.19 ± 0.51 vs. 10.39 ± 2.22; mean difference, −4.20; 95% CI, −4.53 to −3.88; P < 0.001), indicating better mucosal visibility. Exploratory segment-specific analyses showed lower visibility scores in all six gastrointestinal segments. The intervention group also had higher endoscopist satisfaction, shorter procedure time (10.87 ± 1.44 vs. 12.75 ± 0.96 min; P < 0.001), lower water requirements for mucosal cleansing, and less frequent use of additional diluted simethicone during EGD (12.8% vs. 96.8%; P < 0.001). Exploratory analyses showed statistically significant differences in gag reflex and pain scores, although the absolute differences were small. Patient satisfaction, discomfort, and ease of esophageal instrumentation did not differ significantly between groups. No adverse events were observed during the defined observation period.

Conclusions

The combined formulation of simethicone and N-acetylcysteine incorporated into a lidocaine ice popsicle improved mucosal visibility compared with a lidocaine ice popsicle alone during unsedated EGD and was associated with improved procedural efficiency. This integrated formulation may provide a practical approach to pre-endoscopic preparation by combining topical anesthesia with mucosal cleansing. Further multicenter studies are warranted to confirm its effectiveness, generalizability, and safety with longer follow-up.

Trial registration

Thai Clinical Trials Registry TCTR20240606004

entry.title: Does low confidence drive reliance on AI, or does reliance erode confidence? A four-wave RI-CLPM study of chinese language and literature undergraduates

link.title: Does low confidence drive reliance on AI, or does reliance erode confidence? A four-wave RI-CLPM study of chinese language and literature undergraduates
(PDF) Does low confidence drive reliance on AI, or does reliance erode confidence? A four-wave RI-CLPM study of chinese language and literature undergraduates
(XML) Does low confidence drive reliance on AI, or does reliance erode confidence? A four-wave RI-CLPM study of chinese language and literature undergraduates

entry.content:
by Xinran Du, Sedan Yu

Generative AI tools are now routinely used by Chinese Language and Literature majors for tasks once considered the province of individual literary craft: drafting verse, shaping narrative prose, revising fiction. Two competing accounts describe what this means for students’ confidence in their own creative writing. A cognitive-offloading account holds that repeated reliance on AI displaces the mastery experiences through which writing self-efficacy is built, so reliance erodes confidence over time. A compensatory-use account holds the reverse: students whose confidence is already low turn to AI to avoid the discomfort of unassisted composition, so low confidence drives reliance. Cross-sectional and standard cross-lagged designs cannot separate these accounts because they confound stable between-person differences with genuine within-person change. We addressed this using a random-intercept cross-lagged panel model (RI-CLPM) across four waves spanning one academic year among Chinese Language and Literature undergraduates (N = 390 recruited; N = 387 analyzed under full-information maximum likelihood, of whom 298 supplied complete four-wave data). Generative AI writing reliance (GAWR) and literary creative writing self-efficacy (LCWSE) were assessed at each wave. The trait-level association between the two constructs was negative and could not be distinguished from zero (r = −.342, Δχ²(1) = 2.26, p = .133). At the within-person level, declines in self-efficacy predicted subsequent increases in reliance (β = −.276, p < .001). The reverse path, from reliance to subsequent self-efficacy, was smaller and fell short of the conventional threshold (β = −.085, p = .072). We state explicitly that this second result is not interpretable as evidence against erosion: a Monte Carlo power analysis put this design's power to detect an effect of that magnitude at 53.2%, close to a coin flip, so the erosion pathway is undetermined in these data and this null supplies no basis for concluding that erosion does not operate. A direct comparison of the two cross-lagged paths favored compensation (Δχ²(1) = 8.83, p = .003; bootstrap 95% CI for the difference [.020, .218] across 5,000 resamples), with the qualification that this comparison sets an adequately powered estimate against an underpowered one and therefore describes what this design was able to detect. Compensation is the pathway this study establishes; whether reliance also erodes confidence over a longer horizon is an open question. We discuss implications for writing pedagogy in Chinese Language and Literature programs and for how underpowered null results should be interpreted in AI-in-education panel research.

entry.title: The configurational pathways associated with executive function in preschool children: An fsQCA analysis based on gross motor skill development

link.title: The configurational pathways associated with executive function in preschool children: An fsQCA analysis based on gross motor skill development
(PDF) The configurational pathways associated with executive function in preschool children: An fsQCA analysis based on gross motor skill development
(XML) The configurational pathways associated with executive function in preschool children: An fsQCA analysis based on gross motor skill development

entry.content:
by Dongbin Lai, Zhipeng Zhao, Zhi Li, Jinsong Wu, Pengfei Wen

The preschool years are a critical period for the rapid development of executive function in children. While executive function in preschool children is influenced by multiple factors, existing research has been limited by its theoretical and empirical perspectives, resulting in singular pathways for promoting executive function. To address this, the study adopted a systems theory perspective to explore the configurational pathways through which subsystems of gross motor skills are associated with higher levels of executive function in preschoolers. The study included test data from 67 children aged 3–6 years. Using fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), six subsystems of gross motor skills (running, jumping, throwing, catching, kicking, and striking) were treated as antecedent conditions to explore the configurational associations of gross motor skill subsystems with executive function. Necessary condition analysis indicated that no single gross motor skill subsystem constituted a necessary condition for higher executive function in preschool children. Subsequent configurational analysis identified three distinct pathways that are associated with higher levels of executive function (with a total consistency of 0.906 and an overall coverage of 0.496). The development of executive function in preschool children is not associated with single gross motor actions in a linear manner but rather with multiple concurrent combinations of gross motor skill subsystems characterized by “multiple concurrent pathways leading to the same goal.” This is reflected in the three configurational pathways: “a combination of jumping, throwing, and striking actions,” “a combination of running, kicking, and striking actions,” and “a combination of running, throwing, and catching actions.” These findings provide preliminary insights and hypothesis-generating evidence for future research on gross motor skill activities and executive function development in preschool children.

entry.title: Defining clinically meaningful pain reduction after spinal injections using an 11-point numerical rating scale and patient-reported relative reduction of pain

link.title: Defining clinically meaningful pain reduction after spinal injections using an 11-point numerical rating scale and patient-reported relative reduction of pain
(PDF) Defining clinically meaningful pain reduction after spinal injections using an 11-point numerical rating scale and patient-reported relative reduction of pain
(XML) Defining clinically meaningful pain reduction after spinal injections using an 11-point numerical rating scale and patient-reported relative reduction of pain

entry.content:
by Yoonah Do, Wookon Son, Youngjune Kim, Choong Guen Chee, Yusuhn Kang, Eugene Lee, Yeo Ju Kim, Joon Woo Lee

Background

We aimed to establish thresholds for assessing clinically meaningful pain improvement after spinal injections using numerical rating scale (NRS) and patient-reported relative reduction (PRR) of pain.

Methods

This single-center retrospective study included 1,828 patients who received spinal injections at our spinal intervention center and completed a 2-week follow-up telephone interview in 2017. NRS absolute and relative reductions were calculated using the NRS scores before injection and at follow-up. The PRR and 5-point global perceived effect (GPE; 1, completely recovered; 2, much improved; 3, slightly improved; 4, no change; and 5, worsened) were recorded. The mean ± standard deviation (SD) of NRS absolute reduction, NRS relative reduction, and PRR in the GPE 2 and 3 subgroups were calculated. Receiver-operating-characteristic curve analysis was used to determine the cutoffs for NRS absolute and relative reduction and PRR in predicting the substantial clinically important difference (SCID, GPE 1–2) and minimal clinically important difference (MCID, GPE 1–3).

Results

The mean ± SD of NRS absolute and relative reduction, and PRR in the GPE 2 and GPE 3 were 4.5 ± 1.8, 65.4% ± 21.1%, and 67.7% ± 14.8% and 2.4 ± 1.4, 36.8% ± 22.5%, and 35.7% ± 16.1%, respectively. The cutoffs for predicting SCID and MCID were NRS absolute reduction of ≥3 and ≥1, NRS relative reduction of ≥50% and ≥10%, and PRR of ≥50% and ≥20%, respectively.

Conclusions

The NRS absolute and relative reduction and PRR thresholds were established to differentiate SCID and MCID in terms of pain improvement after spinal injections.

entry.title: Hydraulic performance of 14-G hemodialysis catheters versus an 8-Fr arterial cannula in a mock 3-kg small-dog cardiopulmonary bypass circuit

link.title: Hydraulic performance of 14-G hemodialysis catheters versus an 8-Fr arterial cannula in a mock 3-kg small-dog cardiopulmonary bypass circuit
(PDF) Hydraulic performance of 14-G hemodialysis catheters versus an 8-Fr arterial cannula in a mock 3-kg small-dog cardiopulmonary bypass circuit
(XML) Hydraulic performance of 14-G hemodialysis catheters versus an 8-Fr arterial cannula in a mock 3-kg small-dog cardiopulmonary bypass circuit

entry.content:
by Keizo Wauchi, Chisato Ikubo, Hirohito Imada, Masahiro Miyata, Kenji Tani

Arterial cannulation for cardiopulmonary bypass in small dogs is challenging because small vessel diameters may preclude use of appropriately sized pediatric arterial cannulas. Although off-label use of 14-gauge hemodialysis catheters has been reported, their pressure–flow characteristics under small-dog cardiopulmonary bypass conditions remain unclear. This in vitro study evaluated one 8-French pediatric arterial cannula and six 14-gauge hemodialysis catheter specimens—separate side-hole and sealed specimens at effective lengths of 25, 32, and 38 mm—in a closed-loop mock circuit for a 3-kg small dog. A 34% (w/w) glycerol–water solution (viscosity 2.8 cP at 28°C) served as an approximate Newtonian blood analogue. The Stockert S5 pump flow-rate setting was increased from 50 to 350 mL/min; 50–300 mL/min was prespecified as the primary analysis range and 350 mL/min as exploratory. The reported outlet pressure was recorded 1,000 mm upstream of the test device, while inlet pressure was monitored 300 mm downstream and regulated to 60 mmHg; six technical runs per condition were conducted using the same physical device and circuit setup. Within the primary analysis range, outlet pressure was approximately 136–137 mmHg at 300 mL/min; mean differences for the 14-G specimens versus the 8-French cannula were +0.33 to +0.67 mmHg, with 95% confidence intervals from −1.33 to +2.15 mmHg. At 350 mL/min, outlet pressures were higher for all three side-hole 14-gauge specimens than for the 8-French cannula. At 300 mL/min, outlet pressure was approximately 2–3 mmHg lower for the side-hole specimens than for the sealed specimens across all catheter lengths. Together, these findings indicate small observed circuit-level differences in outlet pressure among tested devices within this standardized mock small-dog cardiopulmonary bypass circuit, but do not establish formal equivalence, device-to-device interchangeability, or clinical validity.

entry.title: Comparative longitudinal evaluation of DIMS, progressive addition and single-vision lenses on myopia progression, binocular and visual performance in Spanish children

link.title: Comparative longitudinal evaluation of DIMS, progressive addition and single-vision lenses on myopia progression, binocular and visual performance in Spanish children
(PDF) Comparative longitudinal evaluation of DIMS, progressive addition and single-vision lenses on myopia progression, binocular and visual performance in Spanish children
(XML) Comparative longitudinal evaluation of DIMS, progressive addition and single-vision lenses on myopia progression, binocular and visual performance in Spanish children

entry.content:
by Salvador Solano-Molina, Miriam Carrillo-Pulido, Sonia Ortiz-Peregrina, Francesco Martino, Rosario G. Anera, José R. Jiménez

An 18-month prospective, non-randomized comparative observational study evaluated the effects of different optical corrections on myopia progression, binocular vision, and visual performance in Spanish children. Forty-five myopic participants aged 9–14 years were allocated to single-vision lenses (SV), low-addition progressive addition lenses (PALs), or defocus-incorporated multiple segments lenses (DIMS). Assessments included spherical equivalent (SE) and axial length (AL), comprehensive accommodative function evaluated by measuring amplitude of accommodation, positive and negative relative accommodation, accommodative facility, and accommodative response, and binocular function evaluated by measuring phorias, fusional vergences, and stereopsis. In addition, contrast sensitivity (CS), visual disturbance index (VDI), and subjective visual quality were assessed at baseline and at 6, 12, and 18 months. After 18 months, SE progression was −0.59 D for SV, −0.51 D for PALs, and −0.30 D for DIMS, corresponding to a 49% reduction with DIMS compared to SV. AL increased by 0.24, 0.27, and 0.23 millimeters, respectively, although inter-group differences were not significant for AL. Accommodative and binocular functions, visual acuity, CS, and VDI remained stable, while distance stereopsis improved in the DIMS group. These findings suggest an association between DIMS lens wear and reduced myopia progression compared with SV lenses in this cohort, without clinically relevant differences in accommodative or binocular function, visual acuity, or subjective visual quality.
